question: Which of the following rivers of India does not originate from the Western Ghat?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tapti **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Tapti River does not originate from the Western Ghats. Instead, it originates from the Satpura Range in central India.
 
• Tapti River: The Tapti River, also known as Tapi, originates in the Satpura Range in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows westward through the states of Maharashtra and Gujarat before emptying into the Arabian Sea.
 
• It runs almost parallel to the Narmada River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Godavari River: The Godavari River, often referred to as the "Dakshina Ganga" or the "Ganges of the South," originates from Trimbakeshwar near Nashik in the state of Maharashtra, which is part of the Western Ghats. It is one of the longest rivers in India, flowing eastward across the Deccan Plateau and emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Krishna River: The Krishna River originates in the Western Ghats, specifically near Mahabaleshwar in the state of Maharashtra. It flows eastward across Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh, ultimately emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Kaveri River: The Kaveri River, also spelled Cauvery, originates at Talakaveri in the Western Ghats located in the Kodagu district of Karnataka. It flows southeast through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, eventually reaching the Bay of Bengal.
